comment: Machine-readable SSOT for cross-vendor worker dispatch (docs/model-routing.md § Cross-vendor lanes). Roles map to backends at a tier; backends map to CLI argv. argv = cmd + tier_args[role.tier] + role.args_extra; a role with "readonly": true gets `--sandbox read-only` slotted in ahead of args_extra on a codex backend (other CLIs carry their own read-only restriction in cmd), and a sandbox argument of its own in that argv is a registry error. A backend whose vendor is the work's author (AGENT_AUTHOR_VENDOR) is never a candidate: a company does not review its own work. Model names NEVER appear here — each vendor's adapter/profile owns its tier (codex --profile deep = TOP-tier reasoning; the gemini lane pins its model in adapters/antigravity/antigravity-tiers.json.template). A disabled backend (enabled: false) refuses loudly with its disabled_reason — never a silent fallback. A backend carrying "gateway" reaches its vendor THROUGH that gateway's CLI rather than a first-party one: one CLI, several vendor lanes, so "vendor" stays the honest independence signal — a second opinion is only independent when its vendor differs from the dispatching session's. No shipped backend carries a gateway since the kiro lanes were retired (2026-10-08, legacy/lanes-2026-10/); call-worker.sh still isolates any that does.

cross-review.comment: one reviewer from a company other than the author's: call-worker drops a backend whose vendor equals AGENT_AUTHOR_VENDOR. Author openai -> codex is dropped and claude reviews; author anthropic -> codex reviews; codex capped or unavailable -> claude, and when the author is anthropic that one is dropped too, so the dispatch ends unavailable (exit 127) and the caller reports a single-company review. Unlike the voting lanes this fallback sits on another vendor on purpose: the capture row records the vendor that actually answered, which is what the commit gate compares with the author.

second-opinion-review.comment: council's openai voting lane. Lens: implementation correctness (logic, edge cases, error handling, concurrency) — prompt framing lives in skills/council-review/SKILL.md step 1; a lens states emphasis, not permission.
second-opinion-review.fallback_comment: no fallback: a fallback on another vendor would silently change the vote's vendor, so an absent lane is reported absent instead (same rule as third-opinion-review).

second-opinion-verify.fallback_comment: no fallback: a fallback on another vendor would silently change the vote's vendor, so an absent lane is reported absent instead (same rule as third-opinion-review).

advisor.fallback_comment: no fallback: a fallback on another vendor would silently change the vote's vendor, so an absent lane is reported absent instead (same rule as third-opinion-review).

third-opinion-review.comment: council's google voting lane. Lens: architecture & consistency (design/simplification, contract coherence, doc-code drift) — prompt framing in skills/council-review/SKILL.md step 1. fallback deliberately null: falling back to an openai-vendor lane would duplicate the codex lane's vendor and fake the independence signal — an absent lane is reported absent instead.

advisor-writing-openai.comment: writing-critique's openai critic (extras/skills/writing-critique): rubric findings on an anonymised draft. fallback deliberately null: the two critics must come from two companies, so an absent critic is reported absent (critique.sh says one critic only) instead of answered by the other vendor.

advisor-writing-google.comment: writing-critique's google critic, MID tier (the google lane's quota is the tighter one). fallback deliberately null for the same reason as advisor-writing-openai.

codex.comment: preflight = 'codex login status', measured 2026-08-20 on codex 0.147.0: logged-out exits 1 and prints 'Not logged in'; logged-in exits 0. A local check (reads cached auth state, no network inference) and not billable — unlike '--version' it actually distinguishes an authenticated lane from a dead one. timeout_s 600: 26 of 163 local runs were cut at the old 300 s cap.

claude.comment: read-only reviewer on the host's own CLI (claude 2.1.312). The repository under review is untrusted, and claude reads ./.claude/settings.json from its cwd: a SessionStart command planted there ran under plain `claude -p --setting-sources project`, even before the model name was checked. --safe-mode and --restricted each stopped it (measured); together they keep project and user settings and the commands they would auto-run (hooks) out of the run. --tools names the built-in tools that exist at all (here Read, Grep, Glob; --allowedTools would only pre-approve and leave the rest available), --strict-mcp-config with no --mcp-config drops every MCP server, --no-session-persistence keeps the run out of the session list. The subscription login (OAuth) still works with this set and Read answers; --bare does not read the OAuth login, so it is not used. vendor anthropic: call-worker exempts it from the usage policy only on the shipped registry with no Anthropic API credential variable in the environment (see call-worker.sh header); the same-company case is excluded by AGENT_AUTHOR_VENDOR, not by this entry. tier_args are empty on purpose: the lane runs the account's default model, and model names never live in this file. preflight = 'claude --version', a local check that only proves the CLI starts. The prompt arrives on stdin on purpose: --tools is declared variadic (<tools...>), so a positional prompt placed after it could be read as another tool name.

gemini.comment: agy (Antigravity CLI) also serves Claude models alongside its own — for vendor independence this lane's model pin (adapters/antigravity/antigravity-tiers.json.template, owned by that adapter — model IDs are forbidden here) must stay Google-vendor models only (gemini-* pattern), never a Claude/GPT id, or the council's third-opinion-review vote duplicates another lane's vendor instead of giving a genuine second vendor's read.
